description: We are a group of engineering students from Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS, passionate about leveraging technology and engineering principles to solve real world challenges. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we chose 'Build an Astronaut Mission Trainer' challenge to create an interactive simulation game. By balancing critical mission factors, such as life support, radiation shielding, power generation, and food supply.
summary:
Our team developed “Sol 687”, an RPG-based educational game engineered to introduce young learners to space science and establish a foundation skill set for future astronauts. Through immersive role-playing as an astronaut commander, players assume responsibility for setting up and operating a sustained Mars outpost. The primary objective spans five progressive levels, culminating in the construction of a long-range Deep-Space Telemetry and Network Tower to re-establish communication with Earth. 

Each completed level introduces escalating challenges designed to drive to science skill mastery by integrating core competencies such as survival strategies, resource management, and scientific exploration. To maximize educational impact, interactive scientific trivia is seamlessly integrated into mission execution, enabling players to acquire real-world knowledge dynamically.

By translating abstract STEM concepts into an engaging visual medium, the game offers an innovative alternative to traditional learning methodologies. Progressive problem-solving tasks provide a robust platform for students to apply theoretical knowledge in real-time scenarios, thereby cultivating the critical thinking, adaptability, and analytical mindset required for future space exploration.

Designed as a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, “Sol 687” is an RPG-based educational game that challenges students to manage competing demands—such as life support, radiation shielding, power, and food production—while operating a Martian outpost. Players role-play as a solo astronaut commander dropped onto Mars from a ship, tasked with constructing a long-range Deep-Space Telemetry and Network Tower across five progressive levels by securing supply drops from Earth to enable communications for future human crews. 

 

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ][IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]

Throughout the mission, players are assisted by a Robo-Pet Companion that boosts morale, carries extra tools, and alerts them to environmental hazards, alongside interactive fun-fact pop-ups during scans and construction that teach real-world space science.

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ][IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]

The game unfolds across five progressively challenging levels, starting with Level 1 (“Jezero Crater”), where players scan soil samples from Site A and Site B to identify safe regolith while conserving limited battery power for future construction.

 

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ][IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]

In Level 2 (“Mars Habitat Outpost”), a high-velocity sandstorm cracks the prefabricated Earth glass dome connected to the heated living unit, requiring players to mix local Martian sand with a 3D-printer binder to print thick, radiation-proof ceramic shell bricks. 

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ][IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]

Level 3 (“Kilo-power Reactor Station”) tasks players with deploying a Kilo-power nuclear reactor to power the network tower while balancing internal heating, suit charging, and pre-heating the transmission dish during freezing night cycles. 

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ][IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]

In Level 4 (“Hydroponics Research Lab”), players construct an indoor hydroponic greenhouse to recycle wastewater and grow fresh crops 

 

 

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ][IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]

while balancing water between grow beds and drinking reserves, culminating in Level 5 (“Communication Tower”), where players must investigate and fix a sudden internal air pressure leak before powering up the tower and broadcasting full diagnostics to Earth.

 By transforming abstract STEM topics into an interactive visual experience supported by strategic hints, the game helps young learners grasp complex concepts like Martian soil composition, hydroponics, and nuclear energy while building critical thinking and problem-solving skills. The intended impact is to raise public awareness about the systematic requirements of establishing a livable Martian habitat—including communication systems, safe bases, reliable power, and sustainable food—while inspiring younger generations to pursue future STEM careers.

 

Developed using RPG Maker Z and JavaScript without building an engine from scratch, the game features custom character sprites, faces, and busts built from modular parts and color palettes, alongside maps, events, and core data managed through the software's built-in database. The project blends space exploration, survival simulation, and educational storytelling through a progressive tower-construction system, scientifically backed challenges, educational pop-ups, and an unexpected mystery crisis, carefully balancing educational value, researcher-backed scientific accuracy, user engagement, and an immersive Martian visual design.
